    Compute Pairwise Squared Distances

    compute_sq_dist.Rd

    This function computes the matrix of squared Euclidean distances between the rows of two numeric inputs. If either X or Y is a vector, it will be treated as a single-column matrix.

    compute_sq_dist(X, Y)

    Arguments

    X

    A numeric matrix or vector. Rows represent observations.

    Y

    A numeric matrix or vector. Rows represent observations.

    Value

    A numeric matrix of size nrow(X) x nrow(Y), where entry [i, j] is the squared distance between row i of X and row j of Y.

    Details

    Internally, uses the identity $$||x - y||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||y||^2 - 2 x^\top y$$ to compute all pairwise squared distances efficiently.

    Examples

    # Two 2D points
X <- matrix(c(0,0, 1,1), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
Y <- matrix(c(1,0, 0,1), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
compute_sq_dist(X, Y)
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    1
#> [2,]    1    1

# Compare to manual calculation
# (0,0) vs (1,0): 1^2 + 0^2 = 1
# (0,0) vs (0,1): 0^2 + 1^2 = 1
